value.body: A hospital administration executive handles the non-clinical side of a hospital so that doctors and nurses can focus on patients. Employers are private hospitals, hospital chains, diagnostic centres and some trust and government hospitals. A typical day moves between the admission desk, wards, billing and support services, sorting out bed allocation, patient queries, staff rosters and supply or maintenance issues.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BBA (Hospital Management), BHA or any degree with hospital experience
items.note: An MHA or MBA (Healthcare) is common for manager-level posts

items.label: Work pattern
items.value: Shifts, including nights and weekends, in many hospitals

items.label: NABH-accredited hospitals
items.note: Accredited hospitals need administrative staff to keep documentation in order
items.source: NABH data in a Rajya Sabha reply (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join a private hospital as an administration, operations or front-office trainee, often after an internship in the same hospital during the degree. Larger hospital chains run management-trainee programmes for graduates of hospital-management courses.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Coordinating between clinical and support departments
Handling patients and families calmly under pressure
Working with hospital software and spreadsheets

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: unit or department manager, operations manager, quality executive.
An MHA, MBA (Healthcare) or MPH is often expected for manager posts.
The work is people-heavy and can be stressful during emergencies or bed shortages.

value.title: MHA enrolment
value.note: Master of Hospital Administration only; MBA (Healthcare) and MPH students are counted elsewhere. Based on actual responses from institutions that reported data; the true national figure is likely somewhat higher.
